an1.43:1.2: Vedic _ābhṛta_ is used for something carried between realms, as the soma is brought from heaven by a hawk (Rig Veda 1.80.2). I understand the phrase _yathābhataṁ nikkhitto_ as a metaphor based on transportation of goods ([dn23:23.52]()).
an1.45:1.1: This simile illustrates the mind after being purified through the practice of absorption ([dn2:98.1]()). | From here through to [an1.55](), the theme shifts from morality to meditation. But this group is split over the formal _vagga_ boundary, leaving each half stranded. It seems likely this was originally a coherent chapter of ten on mental development or meditation, which has become divided during the editorial process.
an1.46:1.6: “Unclouded”: free of hindrances due to the practice of absorption (_jhāna_). That absorption is meant is made clear by the reference to “superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision”, which refers to absorptions and the various knowledges that depend on absorption ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj4:4.1.3.1]()).
an1.47:1.1: Varāhamihira says the _phandana_ tree (Sanskrit _spandana_) is good for making cots and seats (_śayyāsana_,  Bṛhatsaṃhitā 79.2), although if the whole cot is _phandana_ it will not conduce to prosperity. The translator N. Chidambaram Iyer identifies it with *Ougeinia oojeinense*, known as the Ujjain desmodium tree or sandan. The sandan’s timber is said to be tough and elastic, and excellent for making furniture. In Pali it is also found at [an3.69:7.4]().
an1.48:1.1: This statement is referred to at [pli-tv-kd3:11.3.4]() by a monk who is afraid he might disrobe due to temptation. Hence, while it is obviously applicable to meditation, it does not directly concern absorption, unlike the rest of this group.
